title: Power Rankings: Bucks, Boston on the rise
heading: 2009-10 Power Rankings: Week 21
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Big Z comes back soon. Leon Powe has started to contribute. And Shaq is apparently in OK shape while his thumb heals. The Cavs, folks, are heading to the playoffs with more momentum than last season's Cavs had.

rankings.summaryHtml: Any panic in Orlando, distressing as Rashard's struggles have been, is offset by two corresponding pluses: Vinsanity is playing better and better, and Matt Barnes might be the bargain-basement steal of the offseason.

rankings.summaryHtml: There will be the usual frenzy over the latest Bynum injury news -- especially since Bynum and Gasol were finally starting to click a little -- but Odom's complaints of shoulder issues strike us as the bigger worry.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Nuggets are dealing with ongoing uncertainty surrounding K-Mart's health, George Karl's increasingly frequent absences and a brutal closing schedule. Major props forthcoming if they hang on to the West's No. 2 seed.

rankings.summaryHtml: The home loss to New York was just one of those nights. The home loss to Boston was more of a reminder that this team, for all its on-paper improvement, is still integrating major pieces on the fly late in the season.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Bulls surged in the second half last season after trading for John Salmons. The Bucks are 14-2 since trading for Salmons last month. Can't wait to see what kind of offers Milwaukee gets for the guy next February.

rankings.summaryHtml: Maybe switching to Durant's shoes really has been the trigger for Amare's ridiculous run. Or maybe it's the Robin Lopez Effect: Phoenix is 20-9 since Lopez became a starter, outrebounding teams by four boards nightly.

rankings.summaryHtml: OKC has set the bar so high that you didn't know how to react when it finally threw in a stinker in Indy. It was only the fifth L in 23 games for a team whose leading rebounder -- Durant -- averages a whopping 7.5 rpg.

rankings.summaryHtml: Interesting question for you Northwest Division devotees: Has Denver surpassed this Jazz team when it comes to claiming the most daunting home-court advantage in the West? I would have to argue yes.

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news: Josh Smith has responded to his All-Star snub by playing better than ever. The bad news: Speculation about Joe Johnson leaving in free agency this summer has become a daily occurrence/distraction.

rankings.summaryHtml: Scoff if you want, but Pierce, KG and Allen looked too spry and fiery in Dallas -- on the second night of a tough back-to-back -- to keep dissing. If those three can stay as fresh as they look now, Boston will be a factor.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Blazers have only beaten one team with a winning record in this 10-3 run, but there's something else notable about the timely surge: It all started Feb. 23 when Nicolas Batum was moved into the starting lineup.

rankings.summaryHtml: Encouraging as it must be to see Richard Jefferson finally figure some stuff out, it has to be deflating for the Spurs to keep looking at the standings and seeing how close they are to a first-round hookup with the Lakers.

rankings.summaryHtml: We weren't kidding last week. Although eight of the Heat's 12 remaining games are roadies, take a closer look at their remaining schedule. There's a total of one foe (Milwaukee) in that dozen with a winning record. One.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Rockets have won five out of six and have played three fewer games than the Blazers, whom they trail by 4 1/2 games. Maybe all that means there's still hope for a decent race for the West's final playoff spot.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Bobs can only hope that the first week of MJ's ownership was no omen. They lost in Indy, dropped an OT heartbreaker in Atlanta and scored just 71 points in Miami, reminiscent of their offense before Jack arrived.

rankings.summaryHtml: Even though they've been unquestionably better away from home since early February, I'm guessing that playing eight of their final 12 games on the road was not the Grizzlies' A scenario for making a late playoff push.

rankings.summaryHtml: You get a full pardon if you're struggling to muster much enthusiasm for the "race" for No. 8 in the East when the teams currently sitting eighth and ninth -- Toronto and Chicago -- are a combined 4-16 in March.

rankings.summaryHtml: Most of the Bulls' keepers have been dealing with injuries this month while almost everyone healthy knows they're not in the Bulls' long-term plans. Not quite what you would call an ideal recipe for locking up a playoff berth.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Hornets managed to split their first 18 games this season without CP3, but expecting that kind of success to last for half a season was unrealistic. This inevitable 3-12 spiral dropped N.O. to 12-21 when he's in street clothes.

rankings.summaryHtml: Last week's most seismic upset? Forget Northern Iowa over Kansas. Try that Clips win over the scorching Bucks. It was L.A.'s only win in 10 games ... with the nine Ls coming by an unsightly average of 18 points.

rankings.summaryHtml: Enough is enough? Apparently fed up after Dunleavy was KO'd when a ball hit him in the eye during layup lines, Indy uncorked a 3-1 week, beating playoff-bound Charlotte and OKC and taking its home win streak to four.

rankings.summaryHtml: Twelve games to go. Only one of them -- April 6 at home to Detroit -- comes against a team that isn't in a playoff race. Conclusion? The 24-46 Sixers will get 25 wins, but don't expect them to go much further.

rankings.summaryHtml: The nicest thing you can say about the Wolves during this ghastly 1-18 spell is that they probably couldn't drop into the No. 30 cellar even if they wanted to ... unless the Nets can win two games in a row for the first time all season.

rankings.summaryHtml: The committee (of one) doesn't want to be so alarmist, but even the 1972-73 Sixers had nine wins by this stage. Philly didn't win another game that season, true, but 9-60 has to sound pretty good to the Nets right now.
